title: The $58.63 Thanksgiving turkey dinner

lines: This year's Thanksgiving dinner for 10 — up 6%, the first rise since 2022.
A classic turkey dinner for 10 now costs $58.63 — about $5.86 a person.
After three years of falling, the meal's price turned back up. (Farm Bureau)
The 16-lb turkey did most of the damage: $23.68, up 10% — about $2.38 more.
Cranberries, milk and rolls all climbed too.
The small comfort: it's still about 8% below the 2022 record of $64.05.
And less than 6 cents of every food dollar makes it back to the farmer.
6% stings at the till, but turkey is the one item you can really shop around — stores dangle birds as low as 69 cents a pound to get you in the door.
What's your Thanksgiving dinner actually costing you this year?

source_line: Source: American Farm Bureau Federation 41st annual survey - Nov 2026
caption:
Your Thanksgiving dinner costs more this year for the first time since 2022 - and it's the turkey leading the way.

A classic dinner for 10 now runs $58.63, up 6% from last year (about $5.86 a person), per the American Farm Bureau's 41st annual survey, with prices checked the first week of November. The 16-lb frozen turkey jumped 10% to $23.68 - roughly $2.38 more than last year. Cranberries (+8.8%), whole milk (+8.6%) and dinner rolls (+7%) all climbed too, while a veggie tray, pie crusts and frozen peas slipped a little.

The small comfort: even after the increase, the meal is still about 8% below the 2022 record of $64.05 - and less than 6 cents of every food dollar makes it back to the farmer.

My take: 6% stings at the till, but turkey is the one item you can really shop around - some stores are dangling birds as low as 69 cents a pound just to get you through the door.
